t: The term Antisemitismus was first printed in Germany in 1879 as a scientific-sounding word for Judenhass, but anti-Jewish sentiment is traced to the 3rd century BCE, and scholars debate whether earlier hostility belongs under the same name.

Religious antisemitism, rooted in the conflict between Judaism and Christianity, was joined in the 19th century by racial antisemitism, which held that Jews were a distinct and inferior race and that baptism did not change this.
Racial antisemitism culminated in Nazi Germany, where eleven million Jews were targeted for extermination and some six million were killed in the Holocaust.
dyk: The word antisemitic was first used in 1860 by Moritz Steinschneider to characterise Ernest Renan’s ideas about “Semitic races”; Wilhelm Marr’s league of 1879 made it the name of a political cause.
ev: Antiochus IV Epiphanes erects an altar to Zeus in the Temple and bans circumcision, Shabbat and Torah study, sparking the Maccabean Revolt
Hundreds or thousands of Jews are killed during the First Crusade, the first major outbreak of anti-Jewish violence in Christian Europe outside Spain
Jews are blamed for the Black Death; 900 are burned alive in Strasbourg and Pope Clement VI issues two bulls to protect them
Martin Luther writes On the Jews and their Lies, recommending a pogrom against them
Wilhelm Marr publishes The Victory of the Jewish Spirit over the Germanic Spirit and founds the Antisemiten-Liga
The Nuremberg Laws forbid marriages between Aryans and Jews and strip German Jews of full citizenship
The Kristallnacht pogrom of 9–10 November kills at least 91 Jews and burns or damages about 1,400 synagogues
The mass murder by the Einsatzgruppen that began in 1941 culminates in the systematic genocide of the Holocaust

f.thinkers: Wilhelm Marr, who coined Antisemitismus and founded the Antisemiten-Liga in 1879; Moritz Steinschneider, who used the word antisemitische in 1860 against Ernest Renan; Joseph Arthur de Gobineau, a racial theorist; Heinrich von Treitschke, who coined “the Jews are our misfortune”; Richard Wagner; Louis de Bonald; Édouard Drumont; Adolf Stoecker; Leon Pinsker, who called it Judeophobia
f.texts: Wagner’s Das Judenthum in der Musik (1850); Gobineau’s Essay on the Inequality of the Human Race (1853–1855); Marr’s Der Sieg des Judenthums über das Germanenthum (1879); Luther’s On the Jews and their Lies (1543); Bonald’s Sur les juifs (1806); Gougenot des Mousseaux’s Le Juif, le judaïsme et la judaïsation des peuples chrétiens (1869); The Protocols of the Elders of Zion, a forgery published in Russia in 1903
f.ideas: that Jews form a distinct and inferior race; that Jews are an alien collective within host nations; that Jews control finance and seek world power through a secret conspiracy; that Jews corrupt a nation’s culture; that Jews are collectively guilty of killing Christ; that Jews are responsible for political and economic crises
f.today: antisemitism in far-right politics and violence, in Holocaust denial, in conspiracy theories in Europe and the Arab world, and a rise in anti-Jewish hate crimes after October 2023; scholars dispute the concept of a “new antisemitism” and the definitions in use
